summary: r2 rerun of the SOLR-18138 ZooKeeper CLI integration test with a working teardown. The r1 teardown failure was NOT caused by lsof absence (coordinator hypothesis disproven): lsof 4.99.0 was built from source into /workspace/tools/lsof-prefix/bin and put on PATH, and the start path then succeeded, but teardown still failed. Root cause is the host container: PID 1 is python3 /supervisor.py, which never reaps orphaned children, so the Solr JVM started by BATS setup_file became an unreaped zombie after the (clean, fast) graceful stop, and bin/solr stop's final zombie check exited 1. Fixed at the host level by running the integration test under a child subreaper (/workspace/tools/subreaper.py, prctl PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER + waitpid loop) that reaps the orphaned JVMs; no patch change and no test weakening. Result: ./gradlew :solr:packaging:integrationTests --tests test_zk.bats -Ptests.seed=18138 BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m41s, Gradle exit 0, all 12 behavioral tests pass (12/12, 0 failures, 0 errors) including the new test 5, and teardown completes normally. Port 127.0.0.1:1 verified not listening before the test.
